memory_candidates.content: For unattended cleanup of a resource whose staleness already gates a live, single-actor decision (e.g. a lock's override-eligible threshold), use a SEPARATE, larger threshold for the unattended/destructive operation rather than reusing the live-decision threshold. The live threshold answers 'should this one waiter be allowed to proceed now'; the unattended threshold answers 'should any process conclude this is permanently dead'. Deriving the unattended threshold proportionally from the live one (e.g. 4x) keeps them coupled if the base is tuned, without conflating the two questions.

To test a script protected by deploy-root-guard.sh (requires its own directory's parent to be named .claude or .opencode) in an isolated temp root without adding any testability hook to production code: build $TMPROOT/.claude/scripts/ and copy the real script plus deploy-root-guard.sh into it by relative sibling path from the test script's own location. The copied script resolves PROJECT_ROOT fresh from its new location and passes the guard naturally; the test script itself never sources the guard or computes a PROJECT_ROOT of its own, so it needs no environment-variable override to be testable.

When a cleanup sweep's per-item output includes both 'removed' and 'skipped, still present' lines, keep the fully-routine case (valid, well within threshold) completely silent rather than emitting a line for it. Reserve explicit output for anything actionable: removed, would-be-removed, or skipped-with-a-reason (e.g. a corrupt state file that isn't yet stale by a fallback signal). This keeps a script runnable at any frequency without the output volume scaling with the number of healthy resources.
